frameworks.name: Shame vs Guilt Model
frameworks.definition: A two-part distinction where guilt is internal (breaking your own rules) and shame is external (breaking others' rules), with the power to choose whose rules to follow as the key lever.

frameworks.name: Asymmetric Risk-Reward of Action
frameworks.definition: When attempting any outcome with no downside below the current state, every attempt produces either a win (sale) or learning (experience), creating upside-only dynamics.

frameworks.name: Fog Visibility Model
frameworks.definition: Movement through uncertainty is only visible one step at a time; additional steps reveal as you walk, not before, eliminating the need to see the entire path in advance.

claims.text: Guilt occurs when you break your own rules; shame occurs when you break other people's rules. The question is whose rules you are choosing to follow, and successful people are the ones telling you it's different once you take action.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: The distinction clarifies the source of constraint: internal rules (guilt) vs. external rules (shame), enabling conscious choice over which rules to follow.

claims.text: Trying has asymmetric risk-reward return: worst case you get a no and learn from it, best case you get a sale. Both make you better. Life gives you unlimited shots while you're alive.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Each attempt, regardless of outcome, generates either a sale or an experience, both of which improve your position relative to inaction.

claims.text: When you walk through dense fog, you can only see a couple steps in front of you. The only thing you can do in fog is start walking. As you walk, more steps become available to you. You do not need to see the entire path ahead.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Action reveals the path; visibility expands as you move, not before.
bounded_by: Does not apply when you have perfect information about your path.

claims.text: When you have advantages or inherited conditions, the correct response is to play them, not to refuse success to avoid the appearance of unfair advantage. Refusing to play your cards means you prove yourself wrong by wasting the advantage, not by refusing it.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Refusing to use advantages does not gain you respect—it only wastes the conditions you were given.

claims.text: Fear only happens in the abstract, not in the specific. When you reach out to a stranger, no matter what happens, you always come out better than before.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Specific action eliminates the fog of abstract fear because the concrete outcome (sale or experience) replaces the imagined catastrophe.

claims.text: When you identify that a single person's judgment is stopping you from making a decision, you must ask whether you are going to give that person complete power over your entire life. Once you name it, the answer becomes obvious.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: you are delaying a major decision
claims.mechanism: Explicit naming of the power dynamic (the other person controls my choice) reveals its absurdity and breaks the hold.

claims.text: Most people do not want you to win. Even if you do win, they will invent reverse excuses (justifications) for why you don't deserve the respect you earned: good genetics, great parents, inherited wealth, good connections, born in America.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Envy motivates retroactive disqualification of achievement when the winner cannot be prevented from winning.

claims.text: If you have no money and want to make money, you should have no shame. Knock, call, email, text, DM, ask. Life-changing doors do not open themselves.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Shame is a constraint invented by people who have resources to prevent people without resources from taking action. Shame is the only thing stopping you.

claims.text: All of this is just an illusion. Shame, fear, and barriers are perceptions that dissolve when you take action.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: If you reach out to a stranger, you either have a sale or you have an experience. Both make you better.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Both success (sale) and learning (experience) move you forward, eliminating the binary fail/succeed frame.

claims.text: Alex Hormozi has completed a 10-stage roadmap from zero to 100 million plus multiple times across software, physical products, service businesses, and brick-and-mortar. Less than 1% of companies finish this roadmap.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
bounded_by: Tested across software, physical products, service businesses, and brick-and-mortar.

examples.text: When Alex Hormozi was younger, his father (a successful doctor) told him not to refuse the medical practice inheritance because it felt like cheating. His father compared it to Shaquille O'Neal at seven feet tall refusing to play basketball because other people aren't as tall. The father said, 'You play the cards you're dealt. These are the cards you have. Play them.' Hormozi never became a doctor, but the principle stuck: refusing to use advantages only proves you wrong by wasting them, not by gaining moral superiority.

When considering selling Gym Launch, Hormozi saw a $46 million offer after the business had been valued at $150 million pre-COVID. He identified one person (a frenemy) whose judgment he feared—he worried this person would think less of him for accepting a lower offer. Once he named that one person as the source of his hesitation, he realized he was giving that person complete power over his entire life and his decision. He accepted the offer.

practices.text: Write down the things that are stopping you and identify whose voice or judgment you are afraid of. Usually it is not society broadly, but one or two specific people.
Stop following other people's rules without asking who wrote them and whether they apply to your situation.
When facing uncertainty and unable to see the full path, take the steps you can see in front of you, one at a time, and trust that more steps will reveal as you move.
Access the 10-stage roadmap from zero to 100 million plus at acquisition.com/roadmap for free; each stage is broken down by eight business functions with constraints, symptoms, and graduation steps.
